rationale: This is a cosmetic recombination of two already-tested archive signals — the gen-5 "ExternalFunding CashDrain AccrualStrain" leg (fmb -4.05, alpha -0.053) with the profitability MIN gate from gen-4/gen-6 variants that consistently *destroyed* the Fama-MacBeth slope (fmb -2.05, -0.14), so the prior evidence predicts degradation rather than improvement.

Another mechanical instance of the exhausted "RANK(accrual variant) × RANK(extfin − Δche)" template, differing from the gen-5 archive winner only by adding dp back to the accrual leg — a swap already tried in gen-3/gen-6 with weaker results and no new economic content.

This simply crosses the weak gen-7 "InventoryDebt Overhang" inventory leg (fmb -1.62, alpha -0.017) with the same "− Δche" financing-use adjustment applied three times already in the archive, and the inventory-growth component is itself a well-known standalone anomaly (Thomas–Zhang) rather than a genuine cross-theme interaction.

A fourth application of the identical "− Δche" financing-use template, here to the gen-7 accelerating-receivables leg that produced essentially zero portfolio alpha (-0.004, t -0.34), and the ACCEL operator will further shrink already-thin coverage (~0.05-0.06) without adding a distinct mechanism.

This is the one untested leg pairing in the batch — the opaque tax/other-accrual drain crossed with the debt-beyond-earnings measure, each of which carried independent cross-sectional support (fmb -3.70 and -3.67) with the debt leg supplying the better alpha (-0.039, t -2.83) — though the low coverage (~0.05) and the archive's pattern of strong fmb with weak alpha on the other-accrual leg temper expectations.

This is effectively the long-corner mirror of already-evaluated signals ("Clean Accrual Net Capital Return", "CashRelease Buyback Discipline") and inherits their structural defect: a MUL/MIN of ranks sharpens only the favorable corner while leaving the short leg an uninterpretable mixture, which is precisely why the earlier positive-sign variants delivered weak or wrong-signed FF5 alphas.
